deed: רשת אורט מכשירה צעירים למקצוע מאז 1880 ביותר ממאה מדינות
title: ORT: since 1880 in St. Petersburg, vocational training for Jews that became a global education network

trailer.text: ORT is a global education network which, by its own definition, is driven by Jewish values.
It was founded in 1880 in St. Petersburg, Tsarist Russia, to teach Russia's impoverished Jews a trade they could make a living from.
According to the ORT website, its founders were Nikolai Bakst, Baron Horace Gunzburg and Samuel Poliakov, a Jewish railroad entrepreneur.
According to the Encyclopaedia Judaica, since 1880 more than three million people have graduated from ORT programs.
According to ORT, after the founding of the State of Israel it became a key feature in the country's education system.

stations.title: Before: Jews confined to the Pale of Settlement

paragraphs.text: In 1794 Catherine the Great decreed that most Jews would live in one area, which became known as the Pale of Settlement.
Jews were not allowed to leave it, and were not allowed to own land outside it.
Jewish merchants paid taxes twice as heavy as those of their non-Jewish neighbors.
Young Jewish men were conscripted into the army for especially long terms.
Crowding and legal barriers deepened the poverty in the Pale of Settlement.
The new factories sought workers and skilled craftsmen.
Jews did not have these skills, because the law had excluded them from many occupations.
By one estimate, about a quarter of Jews of working age had no profession at all.

stations.title: The idea, the petition and the first donations

paragraphs.text: Nikolai Bakst, a professor of physiology, believed that education and training for practical occupations were the key to the survival of Russian Jewry.
He persuaded Samuel Poliakov, a Jewish railroad entrepreneur, that the idea was important.
Alongside them stood Baron Horace Gunzburg, a leader of Russian Jewry, who founded the Jewish community of St. Petersburg and built a synagogue there.
On February 19, 1880, Poliakov submitted a petition to Tsar Alexander II, on the 25th anniversary of his reign.
On March 22, permission was granted to set up an ORT Provisional Committee and to collect money.
On April 10, a letter went out to communities throughout Russia announcing the new fund.
Gunzburg donated 25,000 roubles of his own money to the fund.
The founders wanted to organize vocational education for Jews.
They also wanted to help craftsmen obtain tools and materials and open workshops.
The first ORT committee distributed money to Jewish schools that taught handicrafts and agriculture.
ORT gave loans to artisans, and bought small plots of land that families farmed.
According to the ORT website, between 1881 and 1906 ORT raised over a million roubles.
In those years, according to the website, it provided manual training to 25,000 Jews in 350 towns of the Russian Empire.
Only in 1906 did ORT receive regular legal authorization.

stations.title: War, revolution, and going out into the world

paragraphs.text: Between 1914 and 1916 ORT helped needy Jews, who had been driven from their homes in the war, to find work.
During and after World War I, ORT's workshops and its credit and labour offices saved thousands of people from starvation and unemployment.
The money that had been collected was lost in the 1917 Revolution.
In 1921 the World ORT Union, an international organization, was established in Berlin.
It was meant to coordinate fundraising and to oversee the growing activities in Europe and elsewhere.
In Poland, about 100,000 Yiddish-speaking craftsmen were required to take examinations in Polish only, and ORT gave them accelerated courses.
Starting in 1922, ORT helped Jewish farmers in Ukraine rebuild their lives, the first organization in the Soviet Union to do so.
According to a 1934 report, ORT operated 67 agricultural colonies in the Soviet Union, with 3,100 families, almost 10,000 people.
In the 1930s ORT was also involved in the resettlement of Jews in Birobidzhan.
In 1938 the activity in the Soviet Union ended, and the sources describe the reason in different ways.

stations.title: In the years of terror and in the DP camps

paragraphs.text: In October 1933 the ORT office moved to Paris, which had become a center for thousands of Jewish refugees from Germany.
In the 1930s, ORT courses helped Jewish refugees fleeing Nazism to prepare for life in other countries.
In 1937 the British branch of ORT was permitted to open a school in Berlin, after it had been promised that the graduates would leave Germany.
On the eve of the war in 1939, more than a hundred pupils and eight instructors of the ORT Berlin Engineer School were transferred to England.
According to an article by bpb, in 1943 an SS force raided the ORT school in Berlin, and most of those present were deported to Auschwitz.
In the ghettos, ORT was active mainly in Warsaw and Kovno.
According to the testimony of an ORT staff member, about 4,500 students aged 16 to 60 trained in the Warsaw ghetto.
The workshops there operated until April 18, 1943, the day before the Warsaw ghetto uprising broke out.
In the Kovno ghetto, Jacob Oleisky, head of ORT Lithuania, established a trade school for forty children.
According to ORT, trainees in the ghettos received extra food rations and were selected for labor.
Far from there, in Shanghai, more than 3,000 Jewish refugees were trained at the ORT school.
In August 1945 the first ORT school opened in the Landsberg DP camp in Germany.

stations.title: To new communities, and back to the homeland

paragraphs.text: After World War II, ORT turned to Jewish communities in North Africa, Iran and India.
People in these communities had no way to learn skills that would improve their situation.
In 1977 ORT received permission to operate in the Gondar province of Ethiopia.
In 1960 the U.S. Agency for International Development asked ORT to run technical training programs in Africa.
Since then ORT has carried out more than 350 economic and social development projects in more than 90 countries.
In 1990–1991 ORT returned to Russia, and the sources disagree on the exact year and on the number of years of absence.
In 2007 the ORT de Gunzburg School in St. Petersburg received the President's Prize, Russia's highest award for excellence in education.
According to ORT, during the war in Ukraine hundreds of ORT Ukraine teachers continued to teach their students.
According to the Encyclopaedia Judaica, by 2005 more than 25,000 students a year studied in them
According to ORT, after the founding of the State of Israel it became a key feature in the country's education system.
According to the Encyclopaedia Judaica, ORT Israel is the largest vocational training organization in Israel.
According to the same encyclopedia, as of 2005 ORT graduates made up 25 percent of the Israeli high-tech workforce.
Since 2007, World ORT has operated in Israel under the name "Kadima Mada".
It promotes the study of science, technology, engineering and mathematics in disadvantaged communities in the north and the south.
In 2016 World ORT took ownership of Kfar Silver.
In Dimona, students in the ORT-supported FIRST robotics program produced winning teams that took top prizes at international competitions.
After the terror of October 7, 2023, many Kadima Mada students, teachers and staff in the north and the south were displaced from their homes.

stations.title: The network today, and what was said about it

paragraphs.text: According to ORT, in 2025 it marked 145 years as an international network.
According to the ORT website, it today connects students in 36 countries and on 5 continents.
On May 12, 2021, thousands of students around the world connected on World ORT Day.
World ORT is registered in Switzerland, but it operates from offices in London.
According to the Encyclopaedia Judaica, since 1880 more than three million people have graduated from ORT programs.
Albert Einstein wrote that the work of ORT is an undertaking vital to the continued existence of the Jewish people.

According to the Encyclopaedia Judaica, in 1991, after 53 years of enforced absence

disagreements.question: How many students does ORT Ukraine serve?

claims.text: לפי S15, אורט הכשירה למעלה מ-80,000 יהודים במחנות עקורים.
claims.quote: ORT opened vocational schools in several DP camps, training over 80,000 Jews.

claims.text: אחרי מלחמת העולם השנייה פנתה אורט לקהילות יהודיות בצפון אפריקה, באיראן ובהודו, שלא יכלו לרכוש מיומנויות לשיפור מצבן.
claims.quote: Jews in these countries earned a meager living as peddlers and semi-skilled artisans, but had no way of acquiring the necessary skills to improve their situation.

claims.text: באתיופיה קיבלה אורט ב-1977 אישור לפעול במחוז גונדר.
claims.quote: In Ethiopia, ORT received permission to operate in the Gondar province in 1977.

claims.text: ב-1960 ביקשה סוכנות הפיתוח של ארה"ב מאורט העולמית לבצע תוכניות הכשרה טכנית באפריקה.
claims.quote: in 1960 World ort was asked by the U.S. Agency for International Development (usaid) to undertake technical training programs in Africa.

claims.text: לפי S2, אורט חזרה לרוסיה ב-1990.
claims.quote: ORT returned to Russia in 1990

claims.text: לפי S11, ב-1991, לאחר היעדרות כפויה של 53 שנה, חזרה אורט למולדתה.
claims.quote: In 1991, after an enforced absence of 53 years, ort was able to return to the country of its birth.

claims.text: לפי S4, ב-1990 חזרה אורט לרוסיה לאחר היעדרות של 52 שנה, עם חתימה על הסכם עם האקדמיה למדעים ומשרד החינוך.
claims.quote: 1990 ORT returns to Russia after a 52-year absence with the signing of an agreement with the Academy of Sciences and Ministry of Education

claims.text: לפי S11, עד 2005 היו 58 בתי ספר ומוסדות חינוך של אורט במדינות חבר העמים והבלטיות, ובהם יותר מ-25,000 תלמידים בשנה.
claims.quote: By 2005, there were 58 ort schools and educational institutions in the cis and Baltic States serving more than 25,000 students each year

claims.text: לפי אורט, מאות מורי אורט אוקראינה המשיכו להעניק שירותי חינוך ליותר מ-3,800 תלמידים בזמן המלחמה.
claims.quote: Hundreds of dedicated ORT Ukraine teachers continued to provide educational services for more than 3,800 students despite the most challenging circumstances.

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה היהודית, אורט ישראל היא ארגון ההכשרה המקצועית הגדול בישראל.
claims.quote: Today, ort Israel is the country's largest vocational training organization

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה היהודית, בוגרי אורט מהווים 25 אחוזים מכוח העבודה ההיי-טקי בישראל.
claims.quote: ort graduates comprise 25 percent of Israel's high-tech workforce.

claims.text: מאז 2007 פועלת אורט העולמית בישראל כקדימה מדע ומקדמת הוראת STEM בקהילות מוחלשות בפריפריה הצפונית והדרומית.
claims.quote: Since 2007, World ORT has operated in Israel as World ORT Kadima Mada

claims.text: אורט העולמית לקחה בעלות על כפר סילבר ב-2016.
claims.quote: Since World ORT took ownership of the village and its operations in 2016

claims.text: בדימונה הפיקו תלמידי תוכנית הרובוטיקה FIRST הנתמכת על ידי אורט קבוצות זוכות שזכו בפרסים ראשונים בתחרויות בינלאומיות.
claims.quote: students have embraced the ORT-supported FIRST robotics program and produced winning teams that have taken top prizes at international competitions.

claims.text: בעקבות הטרור ב-7 באוקטובר 2023 תלמידים, מורים ועובדים רבים של קדימה מדע נעקרו מבתיהם בצפון ובדרום.
claims.quote: meant many World ORT Kadima Mada students, teachers and staff were displaced from their homes in the north and south.

claims.text: לפי אורט, ב-2025 היא מציינת 145 שנה כרשת בינלאומית שמהנה יותר מ-350,000 איש.
claims.quote: ORT celebrates its 145th birthday as an international network of schools, colleges, vocational training programs, and other activities benefitting more than 350,000 people

claims.text: לפי S9, אורט מחברת תלמידים ב-36 מדינות וב-5 יבשות.
claims.quote: Today, ORT connects students across 36 countries and 5 continents

claims.text: ב-12 במאי 2021 התחברו אלפי תלמידים ברחבי העולם ביום אורט העולמי.
claims.quote: On May 12, thousands of students connected online and in their classrooms to mark World ORT Day

claims.text: אלברט איינשטיין כתב שעבודת אורט היא מפעל חיוני להמשך קיום העם היהודי.
claims.quote: Die Arbeit des ORT bedeutet ein für die Fortexistenz des jüdischen Volkes lebenswichtiges Unternehmen

claims.text: לפי S4, קבוצה קטנה של יהודים רוסים בולטים ביקשה מהצאר רשות להקים קרן שתסייע להוציא חמישה מיליון יהודים מעוני מחפיר.
claims.quote: petition Tzar Alexander II for permission to start a fund to help lift Russias five million Jews out of crushing poverty

claims.text: לפי S5, חמשת החותמים על המכתב הם שהפכו למייסדים האמיתיים של אורט.
claims.quote: Those signatories, then, became the real founders of ORT.

claims.text: לפי אתר אורט, אורט אוקראינה תומכת ביותר מ-7,000 תלמידים בחמישה בתי ספר של אורט.
claims.quote: ORT Ukraine supports more than 7,000 students across five ORT schools

claims.text: לפי S7, אורט שואפת להבטיח הזדמנות לחיים מלאים ל-84,000 תלמידים ב-47 בתי ספר, אוניברסיטאות ותוכניות הכשרה.
claims.quote: our 84,000 students in 47 schools, universities, and vocational training programs

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה היהודית, לאורט גוף תלמידים של כ-270,000 בשנה.
claims.quote: It has a student body of some 270,000 each year worldwide

claims.text: ב-1937 הותר לסניף הבריטי של אורט לפתוח בית ספר בברלין, אחרי שהובטח שהבוגרים יעזבו את גרמניה.
claims.quote: That was in April 1937, only after ORT had promised that all the school's graduates would leave Germany

claims.text: ב-1937 הותר לסניף הבריטי של אורט לפתוח בית ספר בברלין, אחרי שהובטח שהבוגרים יעזבו את גרמניה.
claims.quote: The fact that it was a British-owned school gave ORT Berlin a certain degree of immunity.

claims.text: אורט העולמית רשומה בשווייץ, אבל היא פועלת ממשרדים בלונדון.
claims.quote: In 1979 ORT moved its administrative office to London, but the headquarters formally remain in Geneva.

claims.text: כמעט 85,000 איש
claims.quote: serving approximately 85,000 people in 78 DP camps in Germany.
